abstract_sentences.text: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is a simple but powerful paradigm for training LLMs: sample a completion, verify it, and update.

In practice, however, the verifier is almost never clean–unit tests probe only limited corner cases; human and synthetic labels are imperfect; and LLM judges (e.g., RLAIF) are noisy and can be exploited–and this problem worsens on harder domains (especially coding) where tests are sparse and increasingly model-generated.
We ask a pragmatic question: does the verification noise merely slow down the learning (rate), or can it flip the outcome (fate)?
To address this, we develop an analytically tractable multi-armed bandit view of RLVR dynamics, instantiated with GRPO and validated in controlled experiments.
Modeling false positives and false negatives and grouping completions into recurring reasoning modes yields a replicator-style (natural-selection) flow on the probability simplex.
The dynamics decouples into within-correct-mode competition and a one-dimensional evolution for the mass on incorrect modes, whose drift is determined solely by Youden’s index J = TPR − FPR.

This yields a sharp phase transition: when J > 0, the incorrect mass is driven toward extinction (learning); when J = 0, the process is neutral; and when J < 0, incorrect modes amplify until they dominate (anti-learning and collapse).
In the learning regime J > 0, noise primarily rescales convergence time (“rate, not fate”).
Experiments on verifiable programming tasks under synthetic noise reproduce the predicted J = 0 boundary.
Beyond noise, the framework offers a general lens for analyzing RLVR stability, convergence, and algorithmic interventions.

claim_closure.claim: J=TPR−FPR determines the sign of the noisy group-normalized bad-mass drift.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (5) maps J to the normalized advantage gap; Eq. (6) and Theorem 6.1 map it to p drift.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1/Table 1 sweep negative, zero, and positive J in controlled coding GRPO.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §8 restates J>0 learning, J=0 neutral drift, J<0 anti-learning.

claim_closure.claim: For J>0, noise changes rate but not the eventual basin/fate.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (9) and Appendix E give the same good-face attractor under the stated ODE assumptions.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1 shows only 1,410-step positive-J rising trajectories.

claim_closure.claim: Coarse-grained LLM reasoning modes supply a tractable multi-armed bandit representation.
claim_closure.method_response: §4 defines finite support and map ϕ, then y/z/p blocks.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Experiments evaluate program correctness, not the validity, stability, or completeness of ϕ/mode clustering.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §8 repeats the abstraction without an empirical mode study.

claim_closure.claim: GRPO produces winner-take-all concentration among good modes and smoothing among bad modes when J>0.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (12a–c) and Appendix I/J derive the sign-reversed inner flows.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 illustrates mean-field paths but no real mode trajectories are measured.

claim_closure.claim: PPO-style importance sampling and clipping do not change the leading-order ODE.
claim_closure.method_response: Theorem 6.1 assumes small η and fresh on-policy groups; Appendix F bounds the modification at O(η²).
claim_closure.evidence_response: The claim is mathematical under its stated conditions; no empirical on/off clipping test is required for that theorem but no broader practical claim is closed.

claim_closure.claim: KL anchoring turns boundary collapse into a unique stable interior equilibrium.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (18)–(19) and Theorem G.6 give the ODE result for fixed y,z and β>0.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5 is theoretical; the training configuration fixes β=0.

claim_closure.claim: Measuring J early is an actionable diagnostic: compute cannot correct J≤0.
claim_closure.method_response: The sign theorem supports the direction under the model.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 gives one synthetic-noise task/model setting; time-dependent/reward-model coevolution is not tested.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The recommendation is explicitly listed in §8.

statistics_analysis.tests_or_multiple_comparisons: No hypothesis test, p-value, effect-size formalism, interval construction method, or multiple-comparison procedure is visible.
statistics_analysis.seed_task_levels: Five runs/seeds are explicit. Problem-level denominator is explicit. Per-seed rows, training-group variance, and FPR/FNR estimation uncertainty are not tabulated.

statistics_analysis.interpretation_boundary: Observed finite-horizon results support direction changes in this recipe. They do not alone identify asymptotic fate, real-verifier J, cross-model generalization, or a causal mode-level trajectory.

final_judgment.single_storyline: RLVR under a noisy binary verifier is directionally governed by the verifier’s discrimination J=TPR−FPR; positive J preserves the good basin and changes rate, negative J reverses learning.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the rate/fate framing, binary GRPO update, J gap, phase ODE, mode decomposition, Theorem 6.1, one coding protocol, Figure 1/Table 1, and explicit limitations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–K hold formal machinery and proofs; L–N hold recipe, noise wrapper, and one data sample. This preserves the headline path but makes mode-level, clipping, KL, and reproduction checks appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Use a single governed scalar to connect an update equation, a qualitative phase prediction, a visual phase portrait, and a controlled intervention grid.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The rate-versus-fate asymptotic statement is theoretical under mean-field assumptions, while experiments last only two epochs and the authors explicitly do not establish exact asymptotic behavior; real verifier/mode-map validity is also unmeasured.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claimed qualitative boundary, state the scalar that changes the update direction, derive its sign in the observable state, and experimentally manipulate negative, zero, and positive values under a fixed recipe.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This pattern requires a meaningful scalar corruption parameter and controlled intervention. It does not replace measuring verifier quality, finite-sample effects, real mode structure, long-horizon behavior, or cross-domain robustness.
final_judgment.confidence_scope: The J sign mechanism is directly supported within the paper’s binary, group-normalized, small-step, on-policy mean-field model and one synthetic-noise coding experiment; broader deployment claims remain limited.

evidence_coverage.method: All structured substantive entries carry physical-PDF page, section, anchor, and basis; missing items are explicitly status-coded.
